subject: bootstrapped confidence intervals on standardized coefficients

messages.author: 1d20fff7e5d7720c
messages.subject: bootstrapped confidence intervals on standardized coefficients
parts:
Hi-

I would like to calculate confidence intervals for the standardized parameter estimates in my model. (Any think maybe they should all be the same?)

I have basically a path model on observed variables which are all directly or indirectly regressed on a latent variable. Something like:

y_act =~ .86*y_meas
y_act ~ b1*x1 + b2*x2 + b3*w1
x1 ~ b4*w
x2 ~ b5*w
tot_w := b3 + b1*b4 + b2*b5

I have fit the model, specifying that the se for parameters should be calculated by bootstrapping.The model output given confidence intervals for the unstandardized coefficients and other parameters that I have defined to measure total effects (tot_w). Is there an easy way to get the bootstrapped confidence intervals for the standardized parameters?

I could use the bootstrap replicates that are output as a part of XXX, standardize them and then find the upper and lower percentiles of interest, but my problem is that I can't figure out exactly how the standardized coefficients are calculated. I presumed that, for example, b1_std = b1 * s_x1 / s_y_act. But when I tried to calculate this myself using s_x1 = std dev of x1 from the observed data and s_y_act = sqrt( estimated y_act ~~ y_act ), this did not give me the standardized coefficients that lavaan gave. Additionally, I would not know how to do this for the additional parameters that I defined for calculating total effects.

I feel like I am missing something very basic here. Thanks in advance for you help.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: bootstrapped confidence intervals on standardized coefficients
parts:
On 04/17/2013 02:30 PM, Jes Coyle wrote:

> interest, but my problem is that I can't figure out exactly how the
> standardized coefficients are calculated.

The best way to find out is to look at the source code: see here:

https://github.com/yrosseel/lavaan/blob/master/R/standardize.R

Look at the function 'standardize.est.all()' and see how the regression
coefficients (op="~") are standardized.

Yves.
